title: Each hand-written technical record of Extending fills exactly one slot of the Go code pattern
when: Run lathe check --json, with the Lathe version that STEGO pins, over STEGO's spec at the commit under test, and read the slot fillings of each technical record of ST-EXT that no tooling record generates and nothing provides.
then: Expects each such record of ST-EXT to fill exactly one slot of ST-PAT-GO-CODE, and names each record that fills none or more than one.
notes: Not automated yet: no test reads the slot fillings. A record with no filling and a record with two fillings are the two faults; the test lists both kinds, not only the first one it finds.

title: Each fill of the Go code pattern in Extending serves an essential record, and no Go file of Extending serves none
when: Run lathe check --json, with the Lathe version that STEGO pins, over STEGO's spec at the commit under test. For each record of ST-EXT that fills a slot of ST-PAT-GO-CODE, follow its implements link or its parent. Then list the Go files of the packages that the technical records of ST-EXT name.
then: Expects each such record to implement, build or sit under an essential record of STEGO, and each Go file in those packages to be named by such a record.
notes: Not automated yet: no test follows the fillings to essential records. The scan of Go files catches code that a record does not name, which the rule says to remove.

title: Each file of Extending meets every rule of the code standard that applies to its kind
when: Run the code standard check of internal/assure over the files that the technical records of ST-EXT name, at the commit under test.
then: Expects no fault of any rule of ST-STD-CODE for those files outside the committed list of known faults (ST-ASR-TOOL03) at the same commit, and no listed fault for those files that the tree no longer has.
notes: Not automated yet: the code standard tests (ST-STD-CODE-R01-T01 and the others) read the whole tree, not one domain. This test is the same check limited to the files of ST-EXT, so a fault shows by its domain.
